result.markdown: --- title: "[time_dependent_auc()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} IPCW (Uno) time-dependent AUC at specified times. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_metrics.py#L765-L918){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python time_dependent_auc( surv, marker, times, *, data=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes the cumulative-dynamic AUC at each requested time using the inverse-probability- of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) estimator of Uno et al. (2011). At each time $t$, *cases* are subjects who experienced an event by $t$ and *controls* are subjects still at risk after $t$. The AUC measures how well the marker separates the two groups, correcting for censoring bias via IPCW weights. **Interpretation**: - 0.5: Random discrimination (marker carries no prognostic information at $t$). - > 0.5: Better-than-random. The marker ranks earlier-failing subjects higher. - 1.0: Perfect discrimination at $t$. - AUC tends to vary with $t$. Use `integrated_auc()` for a single summary. **Higher marker = higher risk** convention: the marker should be on a scale where larger values indicate greater hazard (e.g., a Cox linear predictor, a predicted cumulative incidence, or a biomarker positively associated with failure). To use a *lower-is-worse* marker (e.g., predicted survival probability), negate it first. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response. An `Outcome` or a formula response such as `'Surv(time, status == 2)'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. [marker]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Risk score for each subject (one value per observation). Higher values should indicate higher risk (earlier expected failure). Accepts a 1-D array, pandas/Polars Series, or Python sequence. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Evaluation times where the AUC is computed. 1-D array-like. Times before the first event or after the last observation yield `nan`. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `marker`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped first, along with the matching rows of any arrays passed alongside. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : AUC at each requested time, shape `(len(times),)`. Values are in [0, 1] or `nan` when a time has no cases or no controls. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} **Uno et al. (2011) estimator**: For time $t$ let - cases: $\mathcal{C}(t) = \{i : T_i \le t,\; \Delta_i = 1\}$ - controls: $\mathcal{K}(t) = \{j : T_j > t\}$ - IPCW weight for case $i$: $w_i = \hat{G}(T_i-)^{-2}$, where $\hat{G}$ is the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the *censoring* survival function. $$ \widehat{AUC}(t) = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i \in \mathcal{C}(t)} w_i \Bigl[\#\{j\in\mathcal{K}(t):\eta_j < \eta_i\} + \tfrac{1}{2}\#\{j\in\mathcal{K}(t):\eta_j = \eta_i\}\Bigr]} {|\mathcal{K}(t)| \cdot \displaystyle\sum_{i \in \mathcal{C}(t)} w_i} $$ When $G(t) = 1$ (no censoring) the estimator reduces to the empirical AUC of the binary problem "case vs. control at $t$". **Relationship to concordance**: The Harrell C-statistic is closely related to the time-averaged AUC across all event times. Use `integrated_auc()` to obtain a single time-averaged summary that is directly comparable to the C-index. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a Cox model on the `lung` dataset and compute its time-dependent AUC using the linear predictor as the risk marker. ::: {#012f7f91 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and name the response columns lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(death, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=lung) # Compute time-dependent AUC at three clinically relevant horizons lp = cox.predict(type="lp") auc = gw.time_dependent_auc(death, marker=lp, times=[180, 365, 540], data=lung) auc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` array([0.64152627, 0.5943264 , 0.6023971 ]) ``` ::: ::: Compare discrimination of two models via `integrated_auc()`: ::: {#d2842c6c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Summarize discrimination as a single time-averaged AUC ibs = gw.integrated_auc(death, marker=lp, times=[180, 365, 540], data=lung) ibs ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.6084157733720682 ``` ::: :::
